Good start Faisal.  Thanks for putting this document in Gerrit so we can more easily handle comments/replies.

I'm not sure what this sentence is saying.  I think this app gets the PSUs and PSU configuration by looking for interfaces hosted by EM.  I don't think (?) it uses a fixed path with EM data.

The app does make assumptions about the path of the PSU object paths from Inventory Manager, using a fixed 'base path' and appending a PSU number.
Acknowledged
Nit: changes
Done
Should add something about getting the status of each chassis.  A chassis maybe be missing, might not have input power, might be garded/deconfigured, etc.
Acknowledged

As we discussed offline, I would suggest a class hierarchy like the following:
* PSUManager - one object, handles D-Bus/Entity Manager queries/events, loops over all chassis
  * Chassis - one per physical chassis.  Checks the chassis state.  Loops over all PSUs within the chassis
    * PowerSupply - one per PSU.  Few/no changes from current class.

I think we don't want a bunch of PSUManager objects, because then each one will be doing expensive D-Bus queries and subscribing to D-Bus events.  Instead of receiving events one time we'll receive them many times.  This could increase some of the timing problems we've had to work around.
Acknowledged

@spinler@us.ibm.com Do you think it is better to look for the list of chassis initially from Inventory Manager or Entity Manager?

In both cases, should the code look for objects implementing a chassis interface vs. hardcoding paths?
Acknowledged

We initially need to get the PSU information from Entity Manager right?  To get the I2C bus, address, configuration, etc.

Then given that information we need to find the corresponding Inventory Manager object path in order to get information like presence, availability, etc.
Acknowledged

Note that based on a recent design meeting, single chassis systems will still have 'chassis' in the object path vs 'chassis0' or 'chassis1'.

So the number is only present in multi-chassis systems, but we need to support both with the same implementation.
Acknowledged
What paths does the PSU app publish?  I know it publishes some PSU sensors, but are there others?
Acknowledged
Looks good, couple of questions/comments

I guess to be explicit, "It gets the PSUs device access information and allowed PSU configurations using interfaces hosted by entity manager".  

The psu information such as ccin and status_word it gets directly from the psu itself.
Modified to: - It gets the PSUs device access information and allowed PSU configurations (such as PSU I2CBus and I2CAddress)using interfaces hosted by **entity manager**
does the app get the object path FROM inventory manager, or does it use the object path TO ACCESS inventory manager?
Uses the object path to access inventory manager
please update the sentence above to match then thanks
Thanks for putting an example in there, that helps (me at least) understand it.  Should the example have 0 or 1 at the very end though, I believe the path includes the psu number?
Acknowledged
can you please add a little more information on GetSubTree so we can see if/how it fits in?
Added link to getSubTree and description

I assume at some later time you'll add the details here how to get the i2c bus info from the EM file that is offset by the chassis number; ie the virtual bus number to get to the psus in the right sled?

for "Find all present PSUs in chassis", I believe psu-monitor does the gpio presence detection itself.  Are you wanting to get just the present psu's to add to the vector, or all potential psu's from the backplane EM file to add to the vector?
Not planning to change the existing logic of detecting PSUs, planning to get a vector of present PSUs from the current code.
I don't know the offset at this time, I'm hoping to use the current logic as is and add some offset to I2C Bus/Addr based on the chassis number.
Yep thats fine if you don't know yet exactly how it will work, my question is will it be documented here when you do so it can be reviewed?
So you will get the psu list from PIM after we've already done the present detection and sent info to PIM? Or using the psu list that we've gotten ourselves in psu-monitor?
Another new thing that needs to be done is to associate the multiple PGOOD properties with their chassis, so the PSUs in a chassis only react to PGOOD changes of that chassis.
Added comment to bullet #2 to add PGOOD Chassis to the chassis vector
I assume by this you mean the journal entries, or is it something else?
Modified log to journal

I think you should add them all, and each Chassis object should listen for D-Bus events to track the pgood status of that specific chassis.

At standby all will have a false pgood value.  Also, if something is fixed or starts working again, a chassis that had a false pgood value at runtime might be OK after the next boot.
Done

Currently the code gets all possible power supplies from EntityManager.  I think we need to continue to do this?

PSUs can be hot plugged, so we don't want to just get the ones that are present at the time phosphor-psu-monitor starts.

Also, on some systems it might be valid to add or remove a chassis while the BMC is running.  So the presence of chassis and PSUs is going to be dynamic.
Done
Nit: add
Done

@derekh@us.ibm.com What is the list of conditions the PSU app should check for before monitoring PSUs and reporting errors?
* Chassis is present
* Chassis has power good
* Chassis is not de-configured/garded?

Maybe the second one automatically handles the third one?  Any others?

chassis should be present to send any cmds.
chassis should have standby power applied and not doing cfam card CCM to send any cmds - this is new for multi-chassis (for bmc code).

chassis should have power good for most of the fault handling - eg to log an SRC.  we still poll and read sensors at standby I believe.
chassis deconfigured/garded has no impact on this.  just matters if on or off.
Done
looks close!
Making good progress
nit: still missing the space
Done

Is this a D-Bus bus object?  I don't think it would make sense for the Chassis constructor to take as input an I2C bus number.  While the PSUs on some systems might share the same I2C bus within a chassis, that is not guaranteed.

Modified to:
Chassis class constructor take parameters D-Bus, chassis number, and object path

Since EM will only have objects on D-Bus for things that are present, is the plan for when a chassis isn't present to still have a Chassis object with no power supplies created, or no Chassis object at all?
The plan to have all the chassis added whether powered on/off as suggested in https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-power/+/79980/16..18/phosphor-power-supply/docs/MultiChassis.md#b53
I'll let Matt respond here but I believe he's asking about chassis presence, not about whether it's powered on or not
correct.  Just wondering if you planned to have empty (no PSU) Chassis objects for missing sleds, or just not create the Chassis object until the thing is actually present.
Only present chassis, not supporting missing chassis in a system.

You should specify which service or object path you are using as input to the getSubTree call.  Are you calling this an EntityManager chassis object path, or on an Inventory Manager chassis object path?
modified to say:  ... from inventory manager using getSubTree ...
see comments in patchset 16.  we still monitor the psu's at standby (at standby the chassis "pgood" isn't on, it's at standby), but we only create PELs for the fails if the system is on

It might be implied here, but I think the Chassis object should be checking the state of the physical chassis and then looping through/monitoring its own PSUs.  

The PSUManager object should just loop over the Chassis objects and tell each one to monitor their PSUs.

I think that will make the code easier to understand and test.  Let each object control their own stuff.
modified to: - The PSUManager object loops over all **chassis** that are present and have standby power.The **phosphor-psu-monitor** app monitors all PSUs associated with the chassis to: ....
Done

The PSU app will still need to get the PSU presence and VPD and then update those on D-Bus indirectly using the InventoryManager Notify interface.  The VPD/presence logic should be the same as long as the correct InventoryManager PSU object path has been located in the multi-chassis environment.  Not sure if you want to mention that here.
Done

As discussed offline, there should probably be a section here on the PowerSystemInputs interface and how that will be affected by multi-chassis.  @derekh@us.ibm.com can help, and if this is not fully designed yet you could at least add a section for it with the details as "TBD" (To Be Determined).
Done

Done

One additional recommendation, for later when implementing the changes, would be to save the journal before and after making changes to compare the behavior and make sure any differences are accounted for.
